title: Per-item refusal events let a sender set the log's size
description:
Several WARN and INFO events fire once per item on a path whose volume
a sender controls, so a hostile or broken peer sets the log's size.

| event | level | per | site |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_message_discarded` | warn | received message | mimid-agent-store/src/sync.rs:1036 |
| `live_stream_frame_refused` | warn | stream frame | mimid-agent-core/src/stream.rs:301 |
| `fanout_delivery_refused` | warn | delivery | mimid-server/src/hub/fanout.rs:265 |
| `catch_up_refused` | warn | catch-up answer | mimid-server/src/follower/notify.rs:390 |
| `agent_jmap_push_too_large` | warn | push | mimid-agent-jmap/src/push_deliver.rs:225 |
| `group_info_too_large` | info | request | mimid-server/src/hub/group_info.rs:133 |
| `welcome_too_large` | info | Commit | mimid-server/src/hub/update.rs:945 |

A sender that submits ten thousand messages with a past `expires`
writes ten thousand WARN lines, at the level an operator watches.

## Not simply a level to lower

Each of these is worth knowing. A discarded message is one the user
will never see, and `agent_message_discarded` already pushes the same
fact into `report.problems`, so the front end tells the user
regardless. The question is which channel carries the per-item detail
and which carries the fact that it is happening at all.

## What the answer probably is

mimid has a metrics facility now (`telemetry::metrics`, bead
mimid-ndov), which did not exist when these events were written. A
counter per refusal reason answers "how often" without a line each,
and a periodic summary answers "is this happening now" for an operator
reading the log. Keep the per-item event at DEBUG for the operator who
is looking at one sender.

Per event, decide: a counter, a periodic summary, a DEBUG event, or
some pair of those. Do not lower a level without putting the fact
somewhere an operator still sees it.

## Why this is a decision and not a cleanup

Lowering a WARN an operator may already alert on is a visible change,
and `welcome_too_large` is named in docs/operating.md as an example of
what to alert on. Whatever is decided goes in that document too.

The metrics-label rule in telemetry.rs's Limitations binds the answer:
a counter must not be labelled by anything an unauthenticated sender
chooses, so "refusal reason" has to come from a fixed set.
design:
Answered with a window and a counter, not with a lower level.

Every one of the seven keeps its name and its level. `welcome_too_large`
is docs/operating.md's own example of what to alert on, so lowering it
would change what an operator already watches. What changed is the rate.

`mimid_telemetry::refusals` holds a `Refusal` enum, one variant per
event, with `count()`:

- `Some(suppressed)` means log this one; `suppressed` is how many of
  that event were left out of the log since the previous line of it.
- `None` means one was logged less than `WINDOW` (60 s) ago. Counted,
  not logged.
- The window is per event, so another kind is logged at once.
- The decision is a compare-exchange on the last-line time, so of two
  threads that both find the window open only one takes the line.
- The clock is process-monotonic, so moving the system clock cannot
  open or close a window.

`mimid.refusals` counts every one, by `event`, logged or not. By event
and NOT by reason: at `agent_message_discarded` and
`live_stream_frame_refused` the reason is free text, and a metric label
an unauthenticated sender chooses is what telemetry's Limitations
forbid. The reason stays a field of the line that is written. The
instrument is an observable counter registered in `Telemetry::new`;
`ObservableCounter` in opentelemetry 0.33 is a marker type and the
callback lives in the meter provider, so there is nothing to keep alive.

This supersedes the bead's own suggestion of DEBUG plus a periodic
summary. The window needs no background task, keeps the first
occurrence immediate and at its original level, and leaves no event
whose level an operator's alert would no longer match.

The seven sites, each now one line per window with `suppressed` added:
agent_message_discarded, agent_jmap_push_too_large,
live_stream_frame_refused, fanout_delivery_refused, catch_up_refused,
group_info_too_large, welcome_too_large.

Limits, in the module's own Limitations: `suppressed` reaches the log on
the NEXT line of that kind, so when the refusals stop the last window's
count is in the metric only; the window is per event, not per room or
per sender, so one peer's refusals hide another's of the same kind for a
minute; the counts and windows are process-global, so a test asserting
on one of these lines must be the first in its binary to provoke it.

Documented in docs/operating.md (the four server events) and
docs/agent.md (the three agent events), beside the alerting advice that
named one of them.

Not done: no test provokes a real call site twice and counts the lines.
The window is unit-tested on an injected clock and the counter through
the SDK's in-memory exporter (crates/mimid-telemetry/tests/
refusal_metric.rs). A per-site test would depend on test order within
its binary, since the window is process-global.
